questions.answer: Add a NEW epic-wide flag: FeatureEnum::COMPANY_METRICS = 'platform_repo_pro_company_metrics'. Feature::define() it in PennantServiceProvider (isInsightLpr() || isProEnabled() shape, NO experimental config gate), add it to the CLARITY_PRO and CLARITY_PRO_PLUS lists in ProTierEnum::features(), and override this card's canViewCardData() as Feature::active(FeatureEnum::COMPANY_METRICS->slug()) || session()->has('admin_impersonator'). questions.why_material: Candidate 2 claimed the default seam suffices; candidates 1 and 3 disagreed and candidate 3's reasoning is decisive and driver-verified: canViewCardData() falls back to canView(), which is the same hasAnyRole(ADMIN, USER) check the whole grid already enforces — it has nothing to do with Pro tier. So the default seam CANNOT satisfy this AC. A real FeatureEnum override is required, and none exists for Company Metrics. This card would be the FIRST genuinely gated card in the epic, so the decision sets precedent for the other 8. Reusing FeatureEnum::CLICKHOUSE_HITS is a trap: it is additionally gated behind config('app.experimental.clickhouse.hits'), which defaults to false, so the card would be locked for everyone.

resource_envelope.trigger: New ClickHouse query class (app/Clickhouse/Queries/StagingLiveHitLeaderQuery.php) executed on a Company Metrics dashboard page render

driving_tables.group_by: kit_org_id + month partition; leaderboard further groups by kit_id
driving_tables.single_month_query_cost: 1,514,212 read_rows / 83.9 MiB read / 436.4 MiB peak / 69 ms server

resource_envelope.growth: hits_cold has no TTL and is append-only. Because kit_org_id is not in the sort key, per-query cost tracks the MONTH PARTITION size rather than tenant size — a 2-row org measured ~1.6M rows read for the same window as the largest org. So hit-volume growth, not org count, drives future cost, and it affects every org equally.
resource_envelope.schedule_note: Explicitly none — this is a page-render query, not a scheduled command or job. No interval or overlap window applies.
resource_envelope.allocation_sketch: CORRECTED after the RN2/RN3 fix cycles (all three RN3 lanes flagged the stale record). Warm render: 0 ClickHouse calls. FULLY COLD entitled render: THREE sequential calls, not the 1 this sketch originally claimed -- (1) StagingLiveHitLeaderQuery::handleMonthly() over the 13-month leaderboard gap; (2) HitPlateStatsBatchQuery::handle() over the 12 past shared months; (3) HitPlateStatsBatchQuery::handleRange() for the current shared month (added by the RN2 current-month fix). They are SEQUENTIAL within one request, so the instantaneous per-request peak is max(...) ~1.22 GiB, NOT the sum. FLEET delta: calls (2) and (3) are the four hit cards' own resolvers, merely issued earlier by this card and consequently short-circuited by them -- both guards traced by two lanes -- so the fleet cost for an entitled cold render is 5 vs 4 before, i.e. NET +1 (the leaderboard batch), and 0 delta for a non-entitled org. No existing card regresses, which is AC-4's actual obligation, but the earlier claims 'cold cache = exactly 1 batched call' and 'zero extra ClickHouse round trips' were both literally false and are withdrawn.
unresolved: The BATCHED LEADERBOARD query's peak is UNMEASURED, and the acceptance recorded here leaned on a shape-equivalence with HitPlateStatsBatchQuery that does not hold: adding kit_id to the GROUP BY materialises one uniqExact state per (month, kit) -- 13*K for a K-kit org instead of 13 -- and LIMIT 10 BY month runs POST-aggregation so it cannot bound that. read_rows is partition-sized either way (idx_hit_type is set(10) on a ~5-value LowCardinality column, so hit_type='S' prunes no granules); only the state count differs. Two lanes judged it plausibly at or below the sibling's 1.22 GiB (this query aggregates ONE state per group where the sibling aggregates four, and it does filter hit_type where the sibling does not), but that is inference. No kit count for the largest org is recorded anywhere. MEASURE THIS IN QA.

No concurrent-cold-render ceiling is established for the Cloud cluster. A local QA container died at 5.21 GiB (~12 concurrent 436 MiB renders, CH error 241). Going from 1 to 3 sequential heavy queries per cold render roughly triples the window in which one render holds a >1 GiB query open, which raises the expected number of simultaneous heavy queries at a fixed arrival rate even though the per-request peak is unchanged. The 1.22 GiB envelope itself is operator-accepted per the ticket; this is the amplification the acceptance did not cover.

The QA resource lane must therefore report: the measured peak of handleMonthly() at production cardinality, the largest org's kit count, and the observed per-render round-trip count -- not just restate the ticket's sibling figures.
resource_envelope.allocation_sketch_SUPERSEDED_rn2_rn3: Warm render: 0 ClickHouse calls. Steady state (only the current month stale): ~443 MiB peak, ~69 ms server, 1 round trip. Fully cold render (13 months uncached, once per org per cache generation — past months cache ~1 year, current month ~15 min): ~1.22 GiB peak, 1 round trip, versus 13 round trips at ~443 MiB and ~1.93 s client wall in the un-batched shape. Measured RN5 trade: peak 443 -> 1248 MiB (2.82x) but rows read -21%, server time -2.1x, client wall -5.1x, memory-time integral -44%, cold-cache only. Single-request allocation, so risk scales with CONCURRENT cold renders, not steady traffic.
